checked_claims.claim: Edition, player count, designer and duration metadata
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.12–24; publisher-duration-metadata.json
checked_claims.detail: The summary explicitly scopes rules to the 2014 dlp English 2–4-player base game and the 20 original Place Tiles. Reiner Stockhausen matches the p.24 credit. The saved official-publisher excerpt corroborates 90 minutes only; its current 2–5 listing is not used to change this edition’s rules or player count.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf p.24
checked_claims.detail: All stated quantities match: boards/bags/merchants, 40 stations, 28 markers, 104 Followers, 90 goods with 24/21/18/15/12 split, 16 Technology, 14 Citizens, 47 coins, 20 Places, 18 Hour Glass, two overview cards and Start Player token.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.12–13
checked_claims.detail: Shared supplies, 13 Citizens on marked spaces plus one reserved, five starting coins, seven markers on initial track spaces, four marked starting Followers on the Market, ten stations and Merchant in Orléans are correct. Starting draw allowance four and Development Status one match pp.14,17,19.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.12–13
checked_claims.detail: Original lighter Pilgrimage is on top of the shuffled other 17 events; goods are randomized face down then placed face up. Three-player removals 2/3 per profession groups and six random goods, two-player removals 4/6 and 12 random goods, unused-color removal and 4 or 3/4 empty spaces all match. Category I/II stacks and youngest start player match.

checked_claims.claim: Seven phases and complete final round
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.14–15,20–21
checked_claims.detail: Hour Glass, Census, Followers, Planning, alternating Actions, Event, and passing start token left are in order. The 18th event round is completed, including its event. Pilgrimage operates in Actions, and payment/planning order clauses match.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf p.14
checked_claims.detail: Farmers Track position controls coin gain/loss; unique first gets one, unique last pays one, ties suppress the respective transfer. Two-player last-place payment exemption is included.

checked_claims.claim: Draw, Market capacity, inspecting bag and recovering assignments
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.14,21
checked_claims.detail: Draw up to Knights allowance subject to free Market capacity; unused Market tiles remain. Bag inspection requires shuffling afterward. Each declined draw permits recovering one assigned Follower to Market; no direct Action Space-to-Action Space transfer is allowed.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.14–16,18
checked_claims.detail: Assignments use matching spaces, can be filled across rounds, and require every ordinary space. Town Hall can activate with one. Activated and incomplete unused actions retain their Followers for later rounds. Planning is simultaneous unless ordered resolution is necessary.

checked_claims.claim: Action alternation, passing and tile destinations
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.15–16,18,23
checked_claims.detail: Players take one action or irrevocably pass in clockwise turns. Ordinary used Followers return to bags; Technology remains. Town Hall permanently places sent Followers on Deeds; Sacristy and Tower exceptions are described in their own rows.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.16–17
checked_claims.detail: Boatman coins and last-space first-arrival Citizen instead of coins match. Craftsman Technology is used only after passing. Trader first selects category I, later I or II; newly acquired Place/special ability is available immediately subject to ordinary activation rules. Last character-track space prevents taking its action again.

checked_claims.claim: Town Hall, Deed reward details and marked-Follower restriction
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.18,21
checked_claims.detail: One or both may be sent to different Deeds, each matching exact printed profession. Rewards are depicted 1/2/3 coins, Canalization one coin or one Development Point, and final-space Citizen. Marked starting Followers cannot enter Town Hall or be sent to Deeds; substitution abilities cannot bypass exact Deed professions.

checked_claims.source: base-clarification-invasion-2015.pdf p.3 explicit Town Hall cross-reference and p.24 publisher credit; matching-rulebook.pdf p.15
checked_claims.detail: The 2015 publisher text explicitly invokes Town Hall as the precedent for using any/all placed Followers in the same or separate actions. Combined with the base passing rule, the summary limits this to separate action turns before passing in the same Action Phase. It does not assert a special cross-round partial-use ruling or import scenario procedures.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf p.17
checked_claims.detail: Monks replace other professions for ordinary actions; other Followers and Technology cannot replace a required Monk. Exact Deed profession restriction remains.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.15–16,23
checked_claims.detail: First placed Technology replaces Farmer; later ones any profession except Monk. At most one per Place, none at one-Follower Places, no relocation, and remains after action. Craftsman timing is explicitly distinguished; Laboratory uses usual placement constraints.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.18,21,23
checked_claims.detail: Blue Waterways versus brown Roads, one adjacent connection and one good maximum, empty-connection legality, Merchant location requirement and Orléans station exception are correct. Movement does not itself build stations. Built-station qualification is maintained for income and scoring.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.17,19
checked_claims.detail: One space per Development Point, coin rewards on reaching/passing, first-arrival Citizens on reaching/passing, immediate new Status on reaching/passing Status space, and initial Status one are correct.

checked_claims.claim: End award, scoring and tie breakers
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.14,19
checked_claims.detail: Reserved Citizen only for unique most built stations. Coins one VP; grain/cheese/wine/wool/brocade one/two/three/four/five VP. Built stations plus Citizens multiplied by final Status. Highest score wins; furthest Development Track breaks ties, then shared victory.

checked_claims.claim: All six events and event frequencies
checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf p.20
checked_claims.detail: Three of each. Pilgrimage prevents Monk recruitment in Actions; Income equals Status; Harvest returns food to Goods Market or costs five coins; Taxes one per complete three goods; Trading Day one per built station. Plague draws from bag, returns neutral to board supply, leaves track unchanged, and a marked draw prevents loss without redraw.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf p.21
checked_claims.detail: Available coins paid and every missing coin replaced with any combination of built/unbuilt station, random eligible bag Follower (redraw marked), Development Point without moving onto/past coin space, good, Place or Technology. Items removed from game; only lost Development Points regained. Board/Market Followers cannot be chosen as payment.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf pp.21–22
checked_claims.detail: No action providing an unavailable Character/Technology/Goods tile can be played; availability may return via Harvest/Plague. Coin shortage temporarily prevents receiving coins. Goods-producing Places explicitly require their depicted good in the Goods Market.

checked_claims.source: matching-rulebook.pdf entire English base rules pp.12–21, all base Places pp.22–23 and components p.24
checked_claims.detail: No essential in-scope procedure, printed activation cost, exception, destination, event, end condition or scoring rule was found missing or materially misstated. Optional pregame Place exclusion and expansion procedures are expressly excluded. Track-specific numeric rewards are properly referred to their printed depictions.
